source_review.notes: Checked current Trino, Spark, Flink, and Arrow exchange, shuffle, buffer, scheduling, serialization, and adaptive-execution documentation plus primary MapReduce, Dremel, and F1 Query sources. All thirteen final cited URLs returned HTTP 200. One obsolete Trino exchange-manager URL was excluded before drafting. Product-specific behavior is attributed and generic protocol claims state their assumptions.

evidence: Reviewed producer set U, destination set V, record set X, distribution relation D, hash/range owner, key, type, null policy, and partition count.
Reviewed per-partition rows, logical/transmitted bytes, work, time, skew ratio, and sender/receiver/in-flight/spill bounds.
Checked exchange epoch, logical producer, selected attempt, manifest, modular arithmetic, cardinality, and positive-denominator requirements.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Logical, encoded, compressed, transmitted, spilled, retried, and consumed units remain distinct.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 fixture and reproduced partition_sizes=(3, 2, 1), total_output=6, and every_record_once=True.
Recomputed keys 0,3,3 to partition 0; 1,4 to partition 1; and 2 to partition 2 under modulo three.
Recomputed Exercise 4 mean as 5 GiB and maximum-to-mean skew ratio as 17/5=3.4.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The fixture models integer modulo routing only; production compatibility requirements are separately enumerated.

evidence: Verified compatible hash routing sends equal join/group keys to one destination for positive partition count.
Verified hash exchange requires one destination per selected record while broadcast requires one copy per declared destination.
Verified one selected complete manifest per logical producer prevents attempt-level duplication for manifest-only consumers.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Distribution, balance, durability, ordering, and producer-computation correctness are not conflated.

evidence: Reviewed empty inputs, null/duplicate/huge/nested values, incompatible types/hashes/counts, range gaps/overlaps, and changing epochs.
Reviewed hot keys, compressed-memory amplification, tiny/huge pages, lost credit, cyclic waits, full spill, slow consumers, and gather/broadcast concentration.
Reviewed duplicate/reordered/truncated/corrupt chunks, speculation, producer/consumer/coordinator loss, stale manifests, cancellation, and cleanup races.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Every buffer, retry, retention, adaptation, and tenant surface has a declared bound or failure behavior.

evidence: Traced query/exchange/epoch identity through producer partition/attempt, chunk, destination, manifest, consumer attempt, and cleanup.
Checked required distribution/order becomes a versioned routing and consumption contract.
Checked credit, spill, backpressure, attempt selection, integrity, authorization, retention, and cancellation compose across the data path.
invariant_checking.notes: Page acceptance, durable write, manifest completion, attempt selection, consumption, and result commit remain separate states.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from physical requirements through partition compatibility, bounded transport, attempt commit, security, telemetry, and fault tests.
Checked conditional co-location/completeness argument and its compatible-key plus selected-attempt premises.
Checked credit-bound argument requires memory-amplifying representation and every buffering layer to participate.
proof_review.notes: Necessary protocol conditions are distinguished from end-to-end result validation.

evidence: Audited hash, range, round-robin, broadcast, gather, local, remote, pipelined, blocking, and hybrid exchange terminology.
Confirmed compatible partitioning is not labeled balanced, ordered, durable, or exactly-once by itself.
Confirmed producer completion, manifest completion, selected attempt, and visible output are distinct.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Ordering and delivery guarantees consistently state their producer, partition, and global scope.

evidence: Reviewed per-partition rows/bytes/work/time, buffers, credits, blocked time, compression CPU, spill, retries, throughput, tail, and cost.
Confirmed no universal page, credit, buffer, partition, spill, broadcast, compression, retention, or timeout value is prescribed.
Confirmed production acceptance requires property/differential tests, protocol fault injection, load tests, canary versions, safety freezes, and epoch-aware rollback.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The executable routing example is not mislabeled a transport, recovery, or performance benchmark.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed required properties, partition contracts, modes/topology, pages, serialization, compression, credits, backpressure/deadlock, pipelined/blocking recovery, spill, attempts, multiplicity, ordering, partition counts, skew, broadcast/gather, adaptation, security, cleanup, observability, and validation.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable versioned routing contracts, multiplexed credit accounting, memory amplification guards, durable manifests, fenced attempt selection, per-partition telemetry, adaptive epochs, scoped credentials/quotas, retention-safe cleanup, fault injection, canary, and rollback. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from physical-property needs through bounded transfer and recovery. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover type compatibility, channel cardinality, compression amplification, backpressure, pipeline retry, speculation, range skew, gather, adaptation, executable routing, hash contracts, credits, recovery modes, skew, and validation.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Trino/Spark/Flink/Arrow maintainer, MapReduce/Dremel/F1 researcher, query-engine or exchange-service operator, distributed-systems/platform/SRE/performance/security specialist, affected tenant, governance or accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
